operations.title: Research state for maximal-determinant-23
operations.summary: For D_23, the certified interval remains 2,779,447,296,000,000 ≤ D_23 ≤ 2,982,295,321,444,352. The explicit witness certifies the unchanged lower endpoint, and universal divisibility by 2^22 supports the quotient-rounded upper endpoint. A new exact, replayable classification conditionally excludes every candidate in the specified family of three-edge star perturbations of order-23 Ehlich block matrices from record-level sign-Gram realizability. This local structural result does not change either global endpoint and is qualified by the absence of an execution transcript or a reduction covering all globally relevant Gram families. The exact value remains unresolved. The durable programs are exact-witness-certification, arithmetic-divisibility-reduction, and ehlich-three-star-classification.

operations.title: Three-edge star perturbations of order-23 Ehlich block matrices
operations.summary: This program studies exact classification and sign-Gram nonrealizability for matrices obtained by toggling three edges joining a distinguished center to three unordered leaves in order-23 Ehlich block matrices. The exact verifier reportedly enumerates 1,255 partitions, 1,882,943 feasible indexed specifications, and 102,799 canonical specifications. It reports no candidate at the record square and excludes all 74,896 candidates above it through normalized-square, local quadratic-form, inverse-quadratic, and aggregate cell-moment obstructions. These conclusions are local to the specified family and execution-dependent because no verifier transcript was supplied; they do not alter the certified global interval for D_23.

operations.title: Orbit classification of three-star specifications
operations.summary: Three-star specifications are classified up to permutations within parent blocks, permutations of equal-sized parent blocks, and permutations of the three leaves. The canonical descriptor records occupied block sizes, equality relations, the distinguished center, unordered leaves, and capacity constraints. The verifier reportedly produces 1,255 partitions, 1,882,943 feasible indexed specifications, and 102,799 canonical specifications. The counts require successful replay, and completeness rests on the descriptor converse rather than the implemented set-equality diagnostic, which the judgment identifies as tautological.

operations.title: Exact rank-two determinant evaluation for three-star perturbations
operations.summary: The method evaluates determinants of three-star perturbations exactly from closed formulas for the parent Ehlich block determinant and inverse. The three toggled center-leaf edges form a symmetric update of rank at most two, giving an exact determinant correction through the matrix determinant lemma. The verifier uses rational arithmetic and independently reconstructs relevant 23×23 integer matrices for fraction-free Bareiss determinant cross-checks; no floating-point determinant is used.

operations.title: Exact enumeration at and above the published record square
operations.summary: Using the published record R=2^22·3·5^6·67·211 and the condition det(G)=(det A)^2, the exact verifier compares canonical three-star determinants with R^2. Across the reportedly 102,799 canonical specifications, it finds none exactly at R^2 and 74,896 strictly above R^2. The threshold logic and exact certificate design are supported, while the numerical totals remain conditional on successful verifier execution because no run transcript was supplied.

operations.title: Normalized determinant square obstruction in the three-star family
operations.summary: Universal divisibility 2^22 | det A implies that det(G)/2^44 must be an integer square whenever G=AA^T is an order-23 sign Gram matrix. The verifier applies this exact necessary condition using integer square root and a squaring check. It reportedly excludes 74,792 of the 74,896 above-record three-star candidates. The criterion is supported, while the exclusion count remains dependent on successful replay.

operations.title: Local Hasse-invariant obstruction for normalized-square candidates
operations.summary: A rational sign-Gram factorization makes the candidate quadratic form rationally congruent to the identity, so a local Hasse invariant of −1 at any prime rules out the factorization. The verifier reconstructs candidates, obtains exact rational diagonalizations through two cross-checked methods, verifies determinant consistency, and evaluates odd-prime and 2-adic Hilbert symbols. It reportedly excludes 83 of the 104 candidates surviving the normalized-square test. The criterion and implementation are supported, while the count and detecting primes require replay.

operations.title: Inverse-quadratic and aggregate cell-moment nonfactorization
operations.summary: For a sign-Gram factorization G=AA^T, every sign column must satisfy x^T G^−1 x=1. Cell constancy reduces this condition to exact finite enumeration by cell sums. Of the final 21 reported normalized-square candidates not excluded locally, 2 reportedly admit no valid sign-column pattern and 19 admit individual patterns but violate necessary aggregate cell moments. Integer separating functionals certify the latter contradictions. The criteria and exact certificate checks are supported, while the 2-plus-19 accounting remains conditional on replay.

operations.title: Record-level nonrealizability of the three-star family
operations.summary: Conditional on successful replay, no matrix in the specified family of three-edge star perturbations of order-23 Ehlich block matrices is the Gram matrix of an order-23 sign matrix with determinant magnitude at least the published record R. The verifier reportedly finds no candidate at R^2 and excludes all 74,896 candidates above R^2 through the exact partition 74,792+83+2+19. This is a local nonrealizability theorem only: it does not cover all relevant Gram families, improve either global bound, or determine D_23.
